asset.suspect_interview:
Interview Transcript — Maya Lin (IT) on Last Verified Sight, Issuance Workflow, and Missing Report
Transcript of SPD’s interview with IT staffer Maya Lin about the last verified location of asset AL-77821, how laptop issuance is normally documented, and why the inventory entry listing “Recipient: Elena Soto” with a typed pickup time is suspicious. Includes the credential-directory detail tying badge ID ending 4421 to Ryan Abad, and HR onboarding details indicating Elena Soto’s start date is after the incident.
Interview Transcript — Maya Lin (IT) on Last Verified Sight, Issuance Workflow, and Missing Report
Seattle Police Department (SPD), East Precinct — Case: The Vanishing Laptop (case_graph_rookie_103)
CONFIDENTIAL · INTERNAL USE ONLY
Case Ref
case_graph_rookie_103
Interview Date/Time
2026-05-14 (opened 09:12 PT; interview time not recorded on provided copy)
Location
SPD East Precinct (interview room)
Interviewed
Maya Lin (IT)
Interviewer
Det. Kendra Walsh
Reference Window
Incident timeline anchor: 2026-05-13 19:18 PT
Recorded Transcript (Typed)
DET. WALSH
State your name and role for the record.
MAYA LIN
Maya Lin. I’m in IT—asset prep and support. I handle laptop staging and our inventory spreadsheet updates for the cage.
DET. WALSH
What item is missing?
MAYA LIN
A company laptop with asset tag AL-77821. The inventory sheet line for it calls it a Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 3 and lists the storage location as “IT Cage / Shelf C3.” The row shows it was last saved on 2026-05-13.
DET. WALSH
When did you last personally see it in the cage?
MAYA LIN
During the afternoon on 05/13 I saw it boxed on Shelf C3. The next morning I checked C3 and it was gone.
DET. WALSH
Walk me through how a legitimate laptop issuance is supposed to be documented.
MAYA LIN
Normally there’s a service desk ticket for the request, then we prep the unit, and the spreadsheet gets updated when it’s actually issued. For sign-outs we typically have a person physically present and we capture an acknowledgement. When someone just types a name into the sign-out cell, that’s not how it usually looks when the recipient is actually there.
DET. WALSH
What does the spreadsheet currently show for AL-77821?
MAYA LIN
The row shows status “Issued.” In the sign-out area it has “Recipient: Elena Soto” and it lists “Pickup time: 2026-05-13 19:20.” That pickup time is typed text in the cell.
DET. WALSH
Do you recognize Elena Soto?
MAYA LIN
I recognized the name because she’s on the onboarding list, but I haven’t met her in person.
DET. WALSH
Do you have anything showing whether Elena Soto could have legitimately picked up a laptop on 05/13?
MAYA LIN
HR sent an onboarding schedule email. It lists Elena Soto’s start date as 2026-05-20. It also includes a line that says, “Badge pickup: Day 1, 9:00 AM (Lobby).” So she shouldn’t have had a badge or be doing a pickup on 05/13.
DET. WALSH
Who has access to the cage and these records?
MAYA LIN
IT support staff have authorized access. The access-control badges are individual. Also, the building has a credential directory for badge assignments.
DET. WALSH
Did you check the credential directory for the badge involved in the after-hours cage access?
MAYA LIN
Yes. The credential directory entry I saw lists badge ID ending “4421” assigned to Ryan Abad, department “IT Support.”
DET. WALSH
To be clear, your concern with the spreadsheet entry is the “Issued” status and the typed sign-out fields?
MAYA LIN
Yes. Seeing “Issued” with “Recipient: Elena Soto” and a typed pickup time—2026-05-13 19:20—doesn’t match how it usually looks when we hand someone a device. And with her start date being 05/20, it doesn’t make sense as a real pickup on 05/13.
DET. WALSH
How did you report the missing device?
MAYA LIN
The morning of 05/14 I reported that AL-77821 was missing from Shelf C3 and escalated it to facilities and SPD.
